subject: maths

moments.title: Pythagoras and the brotherhood
moments.body:
Pythagoras founds a philosophical-religious community in Croton. The brotherhood teaches that numbers are the underlying reality of the universe. They study music (whole-number ratios of string lengths produce harmonious intervals), geometry, and ethics.

Members take a vow of secrecy. Women are admitted on equal terms (unusual for the time). The Pythagoreans hold property in common.
moments.takeaway: Mathematics begins as a sacred discipline tied to a cult worldview. Number is the substance of all things.

moments.title: The theorem
moments.body:
The relation a squared + b squared = c squared for right triangles is named after Pythagoras. He may not have been the first to know it — Babylonian tablets from over 1000 years earlier contain Pythagorean triples like (3, 4, 5).

But the Pythagoreans gave it a DEDUCTIVE proof, not just an empirical observation. Proof itself — proving general claims from explicit axioms — is the central legacy.
moments.takeaway: The Pythagoreans give mathematics its method: deductive proof from explicit assumptions.

moments.title: The crisis of incommensurables
moments.body:
Hippasus (a Pythagorean) proves that the diagonal of a unit square cannot be expressed as a ratio of whole numbers. The proof is essentially the modern one: if root 2 = a/b in lowest terms, then a squared = 2 b squared, so a is even (= 2c), then 4 c squared = 2 b squared, so b is even — contradicting 'lowest terms'.

The Pythagorean doctrine 'all is number' (meaning whole-number ratios) is shattered. Legend has it Hippasus revealed the result publicly and was thrown overboard at sea by his fellow Pythagoreans.
moments.takeaway: Mathematics' first great crisis: there exist lengths that cannot be measured by any common unit with another length.

moments.title: Euclid systematises
moments.body:
Two centuries after Pythagoras, Euclid compiles the Elements — including the Pythagorean theorem (Book I, Proposition 47), proofs about incommensurables (Book X), and the construction of the regular pentagon and dodecahedron (favourite Pythagorean shapes).

The Elements becomes the standard mathematical text for over 2000 years.
moments.takeaway: Greek mathematics consolidates around explicit proof. The form of mathematics is set.

now.title: Pythagorean ideas today
now.body:
The Pythagorean theorem is the most-taught theorem in the world. It generalises to higher dimensions, to non-Euclidean geometries (with corrections), to inner products in vector spaces. It underlies metric distance in physics, statistics, and machine learning.

Irrationals are now a standard part of mathematics. The reals are vastly larger than the rationals (uncountable vs countable).

The Pythagorean musical intervals are still the basis of Western harmony, though equal temperament (12-tone) replaced strict whole-number ratios.
now.open_questions: What's the simplest non-trivial Pythagorean triple in n dimensions for each n? Can the connection between mathematics and music (which the Pythagoreans saw as sacred) be made precise? Why does pure mathematics, developed for its own sake, so often turn out to describe physics?

reflection: The Pythagoreans treated their mathematical discoveries as religious truths and may have killed someone for revealing one of them. They were also philosophers, musicians and politicians. The boundary between cult, philosophical school and mathematical society didn't exist for them. How much of modern mathematics' style — proof, secrecy of methods, abstract reasoning — descends from this odd founding moment?
